export.title: Export Replay
export.subtitle: Configure output settings
export.name: Name
export.encodeSpeedHint: MP4 only. Maps to the x264 presets medium / veryfast / ultrafast. Faster presets encode sooner but compress less efficiently at the same quality; Fastest makes much larger files.
export.crfHint: MP4 only. 0-51, lower is higher quality and a larger file. 18 is close to visually lossless; 23 is roughly half the size.
export.ssaaHint: Renders at a multiple of the output size and downsamples. Sharper edges, slower export. Levels that would exceed the GPU limit are disabled.
export.warmupHint: Frames rendered and discarded before the first captured frame, so chunks and lighting can settle.
export.extraRendersHint: Renders made and discarded before each frame is saved. 0 renders every frame once, which is right for most exports: ray tracing and Vibrant Visuals keep time with the replay, and the denoiser keeps accumulating across frames. Raise it when noise or trails remain after the lighting changes: extra renders stay on the same instant and only give the denoiser and light accumulation more passes, so those transitions finish sooner in the video. Each one costs a full render, so the export time multiplies.
export.hideHudHint: Leaves the whole HUD out of the export, so only the world is rendered. When off, the export shows the HUD elements chosen on the inspector's Preview page.
export.recordAudioHint: Captures the game's sound during the export. MP4 gets an audio track; a PNG sequence gets a .wav file next to it.
export.audioCodecHint: MP4 only. AAC plays everywhere. Opus is smaller at the same quality but uses FFmpeg's experimental encoder. FLAC is lossless and not every player reads it from MP4.
export.audioBitrateHint: MP4 only, AAC and Opus. Higher is better quality and a larger file.
export.externalAudioHint: Mix enabled timeline audio tracks into the exported video (works even during timelapse).
export.gameAudioDisabledTimelapseHint: Game audio capture is disabled in fixed-interval timelapse; external audio tracks can still be mixed.
export.rangePreviewHint: Click or drag to scrub playhead
export.multiClipOutputHint: When multiple enabled clips are included, choose whether to merge them into one video or export each clip as a separate video.
export.timelapseHint: Sample the replay at fixed real-time intervals (disables audio export).
export.timelapseIntervalHint: Real-time interval between exported frames, in milliseconds (50–3600000).
export.timelapseTrackOverrideHint: Controlled by the active Timelapse track; fixed interval is overridden.
export.ffmpegUnavailable: MP4 export is unavailable; use PNG sequence instead.
export.invalidOutput: Enter a valid output name and location.
export.invalidTimeline: Choose a range inside the replay with a positive duration.
export.invalidFps: Frame rate must be between 1 and 240 FPS.
export.invalidCapture: Resolution, SSAA, or warm-up frames are outside the supported range.
export.invalidSettings: These export settings are not supported.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.ioButtonHint: Click: set to playhead · Shift+click: jump to point · Right-click: menu
timeline.transportHelp:
Timeline navigation & I/O tips:
• Click the In / Out buttons (or press I / O) to set Export In / Out at the playhead.
• Shift+click (or press Shift+I / Shift+O) to jump to In / Out.
• Right-click the In / Out buttons for the Set / Jump / Clear menu.
• Home / End (or Skip Start / End) stops at In / Out first, then jumps to 0 / end.
• Drag the ruler bracket handles to adjust In / Out, or click them to jump.
